content.content: Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against qwzwpxws, then trxzsqpv, then kwxutvpw; nothing runs, and no behavior is probed. (1) Subject: a decision whose content is still a placeholder or otherwise records no commitment leaves the check with no subject to read — that absence is a finding, named as such. (2) The path form as the section shows it (qwzwpxws): the thing the dependent makes activatable is the path list that decision's Content section presents when content.ref is a list rather than "inline" — the content type together with those repo-relative paths, in that section's monospaced block — and the dependent neither withholds, replaces or reorders those paths, nor reintroduces a body the node does not carry, nor varies that presentation by content.type beyond what qwzwpxws states. Fail on any element that does any of these, naming it. (3) The document the double-click already owns (trxzsqpv): the dependent leaves that requirement's trigger and outcome as recorded — a double-click on a node opening nodes/<id>.json in the editor — and neither replaces, represses nor re-triggers it, nor presents its own activation as that requirement or as a variant of it, nor points that trigger at a ref path. Fail on any element that does one of these, naming it. (4) The activation vocabulary and its bounds (kwxutvpw): the dependent's activation is exactly the two inputs that decision records — a pointer click, or Enter or Space while the entry has focus — as one outcome, with no third trigger, no modifier, no double-click form and no second mode, and with the entry being a control the keyboard can reach so the keyboard input is possible at all. Fail on any element that adds a further or different activation input, treats one of the two as a variant of the other, or needs an invocation the other input cannot make, naming it. (5) No misattribution across the panel's activatable entries (kwxutvpw): the dependent records its own entry and its own outcome, and does not claim that decision's activation covers the Content section or its paths, does not make a shown path one of that decision's listed relationship ids or one of its four sections, does not make activation of a listed id open a file, and does not make activation of a path select and show a node. Fail on any element asserting one of these, naming it. (6) Non-contradiction, licence and decidability: no element of the dependent contradicts qwzwpxws, trxzsqpv or kwxutvpw, and no element requires a rule none of them states — a transport, message, command, file-resolution or path-normalization rule, a visible focus cue or other styling beyond the entry being focusable at all, behaviour for a path that names no file, or a scope beyond what those three record. Fail on any contradicting element or unlicensed rule, naming it and the prerequisite involved. From the recorded statement alone a reviewer must be able to name what would refute it without supplying a rule of their own — a shown path whose activation opens nothing, two inputs on one entry that give different outcomes, or a ref path opened through the node's double-click — and if no such observation can be named from the statement, that is a finding.
content.rationale: qwzwpxws and kwxutvpw are inline prose commitments and trxzsqpv is an inline requirement sentence, so the dependent — prose about a control in the detail panel — uses a natural and a structured prerequisite, and a natural one; the evaluation matrix has no structured-to-natural cell, so this edge takes the default gate form (non-violation of each prerequisite, never a behavior probe of a prose child), flagged to extend the matrix. Non-violation alone would leave the edge ungated in the one way it can go wrong: the dependent composes three recorded commitments that each fix a different half of what it claims — qwzwpxws fixes which value the Content section shows for a path list and that the body is absent, trxzsqpv fixes that opening a document in the editor is the node's double-click, and kwxutvpw fixes the activation vocabulary together with its stated bounds (one outcome, no added variant, and that activation of a listed id opens no document). A decision can borrow one prerequisite's vocabulary for another prerequisite's outcome, or attribute a new entry's activation to a scope that decision states only for the four relationship sections, while contradicting none of them on the surface. The criteria therefore check the composition clause by clause rather than the prose: the activated thing is the path form as presented, the double-click's requirement keeps its own trigger and outcome, the two inputs stay one outcome, and the new entry and outcome are the dependent's own rather than an extension of a recorded scope. Clause (2) also keeps the check from licensing a body the node does not carry, which is the use the dependent makes of the path form. Every clause is decidable by reading the recorded decision against the three prerequisites, demands no wording, order or code-layer artifact, states no rule its prerequisites do not, and names which element or vocabulary fails only in the check's output, so it survives rewording of the dependent.
